findings.title: Numeric IPv4 aliases bypass the metadata block
findings.problem: InstanceConfig(url="http://2852039166", enabled=True) succeeds. The helper at triggarr/web/validation.py:150-171 misses the literal denylist and treats ip_address() rejection as an allowed hostname. HTTPX preserves this host, and socket.getaddrinfo(..., flags=AI_NUMERICHOST) resolves it to 169.254.169.254 without DNS. startup.py:153-160 passes it directly to ArrClient, whose base.py:216 sends the startup request. Thus a configured URL can reach the metadata address this new check explicitly intends to block; this is not DNS rebinding.

members.title: A URL rejected by the new validator crashes startup with an unhandled traceback
members.problem: The new validator raises ValueError for any URL that is not http(s), has no hostname, or is a blocked address. It runs on every instance, including disabled ones. startup.py:192 calls ensure_config() before setup_logging(). The ensure_config docstring at triggarr/config.py:345 says pydantic.ValidationError 'continue[s] to propagate uncaught'. So a hand-edited TOML that used to load now aborts with a raw pydantic traceback instead of the friendly loguru error-and-exit path used for TOML decode errors. Examples: a disabled instance with url = "radarr:7878" (urlparse reads 'radarr' as the scheme) or "192.168.1.5:7878" (no scheme). The docstring calls this intended hardening, but there is no friendly exit path for it.
members.why_it_matters: Upgrading users with a disabled or scheme-less instance URL get a crash loop in Docker with a stack trace instead of a clear message.
members.fix_hint: in ensure_config, catch pydantic.ValidationError from load_settings, log which instance/field failed and how to fix it, then sys.exit(1)

members.title: Config load accepts loopback IPs but the settings form still rejects them, so saving settings silently fails
members.problem: The new model validator deliberately allows loopback IP literals (127.0.0.1, ::1) for same-host *arr installs. The settings POST handler at triggarr/web/routes.py:561 still runs the strict validate_arr_url, which blocks is_loopback. If an instance URL is http://127.0.0.1:7878, every settings form submit re-sends that URL. Each submit is rejected with a 303 redirect and only a log warning, so the user cannot save any setting. The two policies disagree. pending: confirm a later plan in phase 71 is not already switching routes.py to the relaxed validator.
source_window: Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: Users with a same-host *arr setup, the exact case this change is meant to support, cannot save settings from the UI and get no visible error.
members.fix_hint: use the same loopback policy in the settings POST path (routes.py:561) as the model validator

members.title: Metadata-host blocklist can be bypassed with a trailing dot or a non-dotted IP form
members.problem: validate_arr_url_config checks BLOCKED_HOSTS by exact string. ipaddress.ip_address only parses canonical dotted IPs. So http://169.254.169.254./ and http://metadata.google.internal./ (trailing dot), http://2852039166/ (decimal) and http://0251.0376.0251.0376/ (octal) all fail the ip_address parse. They fall into the 'hostname, not resolved' branch and are accepted, yet the OS resolver may still map them to the metadata address. The strict validate_arr_url has the same gap, so this is not new in this diff. pending: confirm httpx/getaddrinfo on the target platform resolves these forms to 169.254.169.254.
members.why_it_matters: The validator's own docstring promises that cloud-metadata addresses are blocked.
members.fix_hint: strip a trailing dot and lowercase the hostname before the BLOCKED_HOSTS check; reject all-digit or octal-looking hostnames

members.title: Config-load SSRF validator inherits known hostname-matching bypasses
members.problem: This diff wires the pre-existing validate_arr_url_config() helper (triggarr/web/validation.py:111-173, not changed here) into InstanceConfig.url as a Pydantic field_validator, so it now runs unconditionally at config-load time. The underlying helper blocks 169.254.169.254 etc. only via exact string match against BLOCKED_HOSTS (validation.py:150) and via ipaddress.ip_address() parsing of strict dotted-quad/colon-hex literals (validation.py:153-166); anything that doesn't parse as a literal falls through the except ValueError branch and is accepted unresolved (validation.py:167-171). A trailing-dot FQDN like 169.254.169.254. or metadata.google.internal., or a non-dotted-decimal IPv4 representation (e.g. the decimal integer form of 169.254.169.254), fails ipaddress.ip_address() and isn't in BLOCKED_HOSTS, so it passes validation here even though common resolvers/HTTP stacks normalize it back to the blocked address at connect time.
members.why_it_matters: If true, a config.toml URL using a trailing-dot or numeric-form metadata address would pass this new startup gate and still reach the cloud metadata endpoint when the *arr HTTP client connects, defeating the hardening this diff is meant to add. This is a pre-existing gap in the untouched helper (config-loading previously had no SSRF check at all, so this diff is still a net tightening on this axis) and is capped accordingly; it is not a defect this diff introduces.

members.title: Rejected URL is echoed in the ValidationError, possibly before log redaction is set up
members.problem: Pydantic ValidationError text includes input_value, here the full URL. At startup this is raised before setup_logging and the redacting sink exist (startup.py:192-198), so it goes to stderr unredacted. In the settings route it is logged via logger.warning('{exc}') at routes.py:600. A URL with userinfo (http://user:pass@host) would expose those credentials. pending: confirm the redacting sink does not scrub URL userinfo and that users put basic-auth credentials in *arr URLs.
members.why_it_matters: Reverse-proxy basic-auth credentials could leak into container logs.
